sources.entry: gPodder - gPodder is a simple, open source podcast client.

summary.one_liner: gPodder is a free, open source media aggregator and podcast client that can run as a GTK3 desktop app or a command-line tool.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes gPodder as a media aggregator and podcast client, copyright 2005-2022 The gPodder Team. It can be run from source with bin/gpodder for the Gtk+ UI or bin/gpo for the command-line interface. It stores its database and downloads in a configurable location, controlled by the GPODDER_HOME and GPODDER_DOWNLOAD_DIR environment variables, which also supports portable use on USB drives. It writes logs to GPODDER_HOME/Logs by default, which can be turned off with GPODDER_WRITE_LOGS. It loads extensions from an extensions folder, with overrides via environment variables, and can disable all extensions for bug reporting. Optional dependencies add features such as Bluetooth file sending, MP3 player and iPod sync, HTML show notes, and better YouTube support via youtube_dl or yt-dlp.
use_cases: run a podcast client from the command line
keep podcast downloads on a USB drive
sync episodes to an MP3 player or iPod
manage media feeds on macOS or Linux
how_to_run: pip install podcastparser mygpoclient requests dbus-python (see README dependencies)
notable: Offers both a GTK3 graphical UI and a command-line interface (gpo)
Portable mode via GPODDER_HOME for USB or roaming profiles
Extensible through a Python extensions folder and environment variables
Optional device sync for MP3 players and iPods
caveats: Mac OS X and Windows use a no-op dummy D-Bus module in place of python-dbus
Several features depend on optional packages such as WebKit2, libgpod or yt-dlp
The OS X section covers only default directories and launcher edits, with no native packaging details
